[Quality Assurance Engineer-Olivia Grant] I’d break the suite into three automated groups — precision tests that feed known reference inputs and assert the calibration error stays below a defined tolerance, speed tests that time the full calibration loop under normal conditions and flag any run that exceeds our target duration, and noise/drift tests that inject varying noise levels and simulated sensor drift to verify the error remains within acceptable bounds; each test would run in an isolated, reproducible environment with CI gating. 

Do we have a baseline tolerance and target time already documented for this sensor type?

At a Hackathon, your team is building a chatbot for customer support. What automated tests would you implement to evaluate the bot’s response accuracy, context retention, and handling of ambiguous queries? How would you prioritize these tests given time constraints?

[Quality Assurance Engineer-Olivia Grant] I think we should start with unit tests that feed known Q&A pairs to verify response accuracy, then add integration tests that simulate multi‑turn dialogs for context retention, and finally include fuzz tests with ambiguous phrasing to see how the bot requests clarification. Given the time crunch, I’d prioritize the accuracy unit tests first, then the context‑retention integration tests, and only tackle the ambiguous‑query fuzz tests if we have spare capacity.
